sources.version: Current User Guide; no semantic edition shown
sources.observation: AWS lists 48.8 TiB object maximum, 10,000 parts, 5 MiB–5 GiB parts, and at most 1,000 listed parts per response. The last part has no minimum. Independently computed: 6 GiB / 16 MiB = 384; 20 MiB = 16 MiB + 4 MiB.

claim_checks.subject: Tus 1.0.0 core; bytes
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Authoritative nonnegative integer offset; mismatch returns 409 without mutation; success acknowledges processed/stored range, not independent final-object verification.

claim_checks.subject: Tus extension support
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Creation, expiration, checksum, termination and concatenation are optional; auth/durable state/UUID create semantics are not implied by extension advertisement.

claim_checks.subject: Tus expiration; absolute 30 days
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Upload-Expires on PATCH and creation when known; known expired resource uses 410. Thirty days is a chosen policy, not a protocol default.

claim_checks.subject: Tus PATCH-body integrity
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Advertised algorithms; at least sha1 if implemented; verifies request body, not assembled full-file hash.

claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart IDs and parts
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Upload ID + per-part ETag/number manifest; numbered parts assembled in ascending order; same-number replacement; incomplete operations differ from object completion.

claim_checks.subject: AWS ListParts; 1,000 results
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Paginate; omitted unfinished calls are not failed calls; retain own completion manifest. Listing alone cannot settle operation uncertainty.

claim_checks.subject: AWS part sizes/count; MiB/GiB
claim_checks.governing_conditions: 5 MiB–5 GiB with last-part minimum exception; 10,000 parts. 6 GiB gives 384 full parts; 20 MiB gives 16+4 MiB. Not vendor/performance proof.

claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart checksums
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Overview states a broad checksum rule; dedicated integrity guidance scopes the important note to composite/part-level checksums. Proposed consecutive numbering is safe regardless; broader explanatory applicability is not settled by the overview alone.

claim_checks.subject: ETag and full-file SHA-256
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Multipart ETag not assumed full-file MD5; storage-validated strong digest must describe the exact full byte sequence, or read-back SHA-256; CRC/composite cannot substitute silently.

claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart SHA-256 versus full-object CRC
claim_checks.governing_conditions: SHA-256 composite; CRC64NVME/CRC32/CRC32C support full-object type. Algorithm/type/initiation/completion/retrieval must be qualified together.

claim_checks.subject: AWS SSE-KMS permissions
claim_checks.governing_conditions: GenerateDataKey and Decrypt conditions; checksum access depends on permissions. Exact mode and permission path gate implementation.

claim_checks.subject: AWS SSE-C completion checksums
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Overview's checksum availability claim is supported in its context. API headers are conditional on checksum use/policy and SSE-C is unsupported in directory buckets. No blanket claim about the unspecified vendor is made.

claim_checks.subject: AWS in-flight UploadPart
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Unknown is not Failed; prevent same-number overlap and completion, settle or retire ID, preserve cleanup queue. Already in-flight requests can finish after abort; repeat cleanup/verify.

claim_checks.subject: Remote object versus HTTP result
claim_checks.governing_conditions: Actual operation success plus target/size/session checks required; AWS 200 can embed error. Final does not use HTTP status alone or cancel intent as proof of committed/aborted state.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: The prior text already made SHA-256 comparison conditional and offered read-back, so the critic correctly classifies missing algorithm/encryption conditions as incomplete rather than a flat false universal claim. Final adds checksum-type/permission distinctions and preserves explicit unverified status.

Draft said query known storage state but did not define how absence from a list fails to settle an unfinished request. Final adds per-operation states, no overlap/commit while unknown, settlement or retirement and retained cleanup ownership. Conservative retirement is explicitly a design choice.
